back: A one-off, temporary undertaking with a clear objective, a start and end date, a budget and resources.
Identification, formulation (proposal and plan), implementation, evaluation.
A written document presenting a project idea for approval or funding: objective, need, activities, resources, cost, benefits and risks.
A detailed statement of what will be done, by whom, when and at what cost, including the budget.
Demand, start-up cost, skills, resources and timing, risk and fit with objectives.
A table giving each project idea a score on weighted criteria; the weighted totals are compared. Scores and weights are judgements.
A reserve in the budget for unexpected costs, often a percentage of the planned cost.
Compare results with the objective, time and budget; find causes of problems; record lessons for future projects.
